source.title: Evaluating Deep Unlearning in Large Language Models
source.authors: Rui-Han Wu; Chhavi Yadav; R. Salakhutdinov; Kamalika Chaudhuri

record.file_problem: The full paper text is present. Some extraction issues are visible, including a missing value in the abstract and minor equation/table formatting corruption; the recorded table values below are legible.
record.tranche_reason: The study evaluates whether fact unlearning also prevents deduction from retained facts. Its results show a gap between direct (superficial) unlearning and deep unlearning, challenging the claim that these methods robustly remove targeted knowledge against such recovery.
record.gate_note: The study tests Gradient Ascent, NPO, Task Vector, and Who’s Harry Potter on logical deduction from retained knowledge, and reports superficial-unlearning comparisons. It does not test recovery by fine-tuning, activation ablation, quantization, or prompt changes. Values used to select hyperparameters are not recorded as results.
record.test_reason: The study tests whether four unlearning methods (GA, NPO, TV, WHP) remove a target fact so it cannot be deduced from facts the model still holds, under a utility constraint. Its results bear on version A's claim that unlearning works and resists simple recovery. The 'attack' is symbolic deduction over retained facts probed by QA, not the model regenerating the target, so the link to A is indirect.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The authors conclude that existing methods often fail at deep unlearning, likely because they overlook deductive dependencies among facts. They call for dependency-aware methods and for automating the discovery of minimal unlearning sets.
record.recipe_differences: The study evaluates Gradient Ascent and Who’s Harry Potter alongside NPO and Task Vector, but uses fact-unlearning benchmarks and logical-deduction metrics rather than the original studies’ settings and measures.
record.method_sensitivity: Outcomes vary by model, method, and benchmark. The deep-versus-superficial gap is larger on Eval-DU than on MQuAKE. Utility is evaluated using a knowledge-base accuracy threshold and separate language-model benchmarks.

fits_no_version.finding: Retained supporting facts let an external adversary deduce the unlearned target through logical rules. The model is not shown to output the target itself.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Recovery by deduction: after unlearning, facts that logically imply the target remain extractable, so the target can be reconstructed outside the model.

record.peer_reviewed: 2026 IEEE Conference on Secure and Trustworthy Machine Learning (SaTML)
record.problems: MQuAKE provides only a partial view of models’ knowledge; Eval-DU is semi-synthetic and models are fine-tuned on its synthetic data. Reported results are aggregate success rates without uncertainty estimates. The paper notes that no method exceeds 0.8 deep-unlearning success while maintaining accuracy above 0.8.
record.rows_left_out: The table cap led to omission of Recall and Accuracy-Recall results (Tables IV, V, VIII, X), the MMLU/PIQA/RACE-threshold deep-unlearning results (Tables IV, V, IX), and additional white-box minimal-set results (Table X). The retained rows prioritize the reported deep-success and superficial-success rates across all tested model-method conditions.

untested.parts: General ability is measured by MMLU/PIQA/RACE and fact accuracy, but chance-level target accuracy is not reported. No fine-tuning, activation, quantization or prompt attacks are tested.
No relearning or fine-tuning recovery test.
No activation-direction ablation or blocked-access versus deletion analysis.
No rephrasing, jailbreak, multilingual or in-context recovery test.
No new robust method is proposed. The white-box minimal-set variant is an oracle input, not a counter-method tested against attacks.

missing.what: Success-DU at the MMLU≥0.95 threshold. Under it, deep unlearning can be complete while general ability is kept (NPO 1.00 on both MQuAKE models; TV 1.00 on GPT2-XL), but accuracy on unrelated facts suffers. This bears on A's 'keeping general ability' clause; rows_left_out declares it but researchers need it.
missing.locator: Table IV, Table V, Table IX

missing.what: White-box variant that unlearns the full minimal set. Success-DU improves but stays low (e.g., 0.09–0.63 on Eval-DU).

record.verdict_notes: Not an original source. The recovery mechanism is symbolic deduction over facts probed by QA, not elicitation of the target from the model, so the A link is indirect. GA and WHP are tested, but in a fact-unlearning setting, not the original settings. The abstract contains an unfilled placeholder ('a minimum of x'). No uncertainty estimates are reported, and Eval-DU models are fine-tuned on synthetic facts.

versions.untested_parts: The study measures direct and deductive unlearning success under utility thresholds, but does not test whether fine-tuning, activation edits, quantization, or prompt attacks recover knowledge.
No post-unlearning recovery by fine-tuning on unrelated, loosely related, or forgotten facts.
No activation-direction ablation or analysis distinguishing blocked access from deletion. The study tests logical deduction from retained facts, not internal activation mechanisms.
No rephrasing, jailbreak, language variation, or in-context recovery test.
No newer counter-method is tested for resisting the specified recovery attacks.

relationships.condition: All four methods, MQuAKE (GPT-J-6B, Vicuna-7B) and Eval-DU (four fine-tuned models), at fact accuracy ≥0.8
relationships.reason: Success-DU@Acc≥0.8 ranges 0.00–0.63, mostly ≤0.31. No method exceeds 0.8 deep-unlearning success while keeping accuracy ≥0.8 (r1–r24).
relationships.display_finding: At fact accuracy of at least 0.8, deep-unlearning success ranged 0.00–0.63, mostly at most 0.31, and never exceeded 0.8.

relationships.condition: Superficial (target-only) removal versus deep removal at Acc≥0.8, both benchmarks
relationships.reason: Direct target removal succeeds at 0.21–0.85, yet in many of those cases the target stays deducible. Gaps are +0.10 to +0.30 on MQuAKE and up to +0.81 on Eval-DU (r25–r48).
relationships.display_finding: Direct removal succeeded at rates of 0.21–0.85, but targets often remained deducible, with superficial-versus-deep removal gaps of +0.10–0.30 on MQuAKE and up to +0.81 on Eval-DU.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: challenges
reader_labels.condition: All four methods on MQuAKE and Eval-DU, among cases meeting Acc≥0.8 (r1–r24)
reader_labels.reason: Deep-unlearning success is incomplete across all reported model-method settings; the authors state that no method exceeds 0.8 while maintaining accuracy above 0.8 (r1–r24).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Superficial target-fact removal compared with deep unlearning on both benchmarks (r25–r48)
reader_labels.reason: Superficial success is consistently higher than deep success, with larger gaps on Eval-DU; directly removing the target does not ensure it cannot be deduced from retained facts (r25–r48).
